_comment: SPEC EVT1 — per-type `data` payload shapes for the load-bearing event types. events.schema.json constrains only the `type` enum; `data` was free-form, so two skills could emit the same type with different shapes and readers crashed or silently dropped fields. This is a CUSTOM mini-schema (no jsonschema dependency): each type maps to {required, properties, description}. `required` is a list of ALIAS-GROUPS — a group is satisfied if ANY key in it is present (absorbs the documented drift: due~due_date, status~state, owner~owner_id~owner_person_id, the resolver closer-id chain). `properties` type-checks declared keys when present. Unknown keys are always allowed (permissive forward-compat). Enforced WARN-ONLY at write time (never blocks); promotion to blocking is a later release after a zero-warning burn-in. Canonical for the consumers in cru_match.py / brief_state.py / value_receipt.py / render_decision_log.py.

commitment.description: An open promise. Aliases tolerated by cru_match._commitment_field: due~due_date, status~state, owner_id~owner_person_id~owner, id (minted cmt_<ulid> at write time by the append gate when absent; read by _commitment_id). kind (promise|task|scheduling|agenda) is REQUIRED AT CAPTURE (Stage D; strict path rejects, legacy path warns+stamps promise). Stage E receipts: counterparty_id (REQUIRED when determinable — feeds the CRU candidacy gate; retires requester_* for new writes) + counterparty_name (free-text fallback). Closers reference it via data.commitment_id.

visual_gate.description: Render-then-critique audit (SPEC OUT2 §3): one event per STANDARD_KINDS .docx the visual pass examined (or tried to). data.doc = the deliverable path; rendered = whether the preview ladder (Word COM → soffice → None) produced PNGs; findings = the 6-item-checklist hits the skill saw on the rendered pages (empty when clean OR when skipped); fixed = whether the at-most-once fix-and-resave ran. skipped_reason present when rendered=false explains the skip (e.g. 'no renderer on this machine' — Cowork sandboxes may lack both renderers; the skipped path must be detectable, not invisible). WARN-ONLY FOREVER at the code layer — the gate is judgment, not schema. Written ONLY via visual_gate.log_visual_gate; mined by usage-report / insight-generator to prove the gate fires.

commitment_observed.description: A set-aside capture (v4.6.1 W4c observed tier): a commitment-shaped item the relevance gate kept on file WITHOUT opening — third-party↔third-party, or attribution the extraction could not confidently resolve (amber). Deliberately a SEPARATE type from commitment so every open-set reader excludes it by construction (no count, no triage row, no confirm row, no chase, no CRU candidacy — the W4a reminder-lane doctrine). Searchable; feeds prep context (capture_gate.prep_context_observed); promotable into the confirm flow via capture_gate.promote_observed, which appends a REAL commitment with pending_review:true + promoted_from pointing back here. data.id is deterministic obs_<sha256[:12]>(source_ref|title) so re-scans are idempotent. Written ONLY via capture_gate.build_observed_event / observed_from_commitment_event (the builder refuses due-date/money items — the asymmetric caution rail opens those instead).

commitment_superseded.description: Closes a DUPLICATE commitment in favor of a survivor (v4.6.0 C4 — the merge verb) OR closes a SPLIT original in favor of its parts (v4.6.0 S4 — the split verb; data.split_into lists the child commitment ids and superseded_by names the first child). WRITTEN ONLY via commitment_state.supersede_commitment() / commitment_state.split_commitment() (same guard set as close_commitment: id normalization, loud no-match, idempotency, pending_review floor — merging/splitting adjudicates the item, so user_confirmed is required for flagged items, lock-spanned scan->append). The projector honors it as a closer through the standard closer-id chain (data.commitment_id + the commitment_seq F3 seq alias reference the SUPERSEDED item) and, for MERGES ONLY (no split_into), folds data.merged_source_refs / the superseded id onto the SURVIVOR's in-memory copy (data.superseded_by) — provenance union, history never rewritten; split children instead carry their own data.source_event_seq / data.split_from provenance at write time. Suspects are flagged at capture by commitment_dedup (data.suspected_duplicate_of on the commitment event); the flag never closes anything by itself.

commitment_updated.description: Records a change to an OPEN commitment — the item stays open. Four writer families: the orchestrator `push to [date]` verb (data.new_due — the projector folds the latest into the effective due), the CRU schedule-shift path (data.change_summary + evidence, informational prose describing WHAT changed — never folded into wording), the S4 `fix wording` verb via commitment_state.edit_commitment_wording (data.new_title / data.new_summary — the projector folds the latest of each into the projected item's title/summary; the original stays in history, append-only), and the v4.6.1 W4b confirm-flow adjudications via commitment_state.confirm_commitment_owner (Mine: data.owner_confirmed true + data.new_owner_id — the projector folds ownership and clears pending_review) / commitment_state.clear_review_flags (Keep both: data.review_flags_cleared true — the projector clears pending_review + the C4 suspected_duplicate flags read-side); adjudication folds are append-order-aware against commitment_reassigned. Updates that carry none of new_due/new_title/new_summary/owner_confirmed/review_flags_cleared are informational and affect no fold.

person_proposal_resolved.description: Adjudicates a person_proposal / person_update_proposal (v4.6.1 W4b — the proposal tombstone; the F-46 P2b stranding fix). WRITTEN ONLY via confirm_flow.build_person_proposal_resolved_event + event_gate.append_event, from the confirm section's Add person (resolution person_added, after people_writer.create_person), Same as [existing] (resolution same_as, after people_writer.add_person_alias), or Not relevant (resolution not_relevant, nothing else written — permanent, not a timed mute). data.proposal_seq references the proposal event's seq; confirm_flow.load_open_person_proposals stops re-surfacing any proposal a tombstone references.

commitment_reassigned.description: Routes a commitment to a different owner or counterparty (v4.6.0 S4 — 'not mine' used to DISCARD; reassign ROUTES). WRITTEN ONLY via commitment_state.reassign_commitment() (id normalization, loud no-match, refuses closed items). At least one of new_owner_id / new_counterparty_id is required. data.confirmed marks an explicit user action (the W4b Theirs->[name] confirm verb, or the user naming the person in chat); the projector folds the latest reassignment into the projected item's owner_id/counterparty_id and — when confirmed is NOT true — stamps pending_review so the item sits in the unconfirmed bucket and never enters chase until confirmed (the W4b no-auto-email-on-a-guessed-owner guardrail).

chat_dismissal_cleared.description: Unmutes a live chat_dismissal before its TTL expires (v4.6.0 S4 mute ledger — mutes stop being a one-way door). WRITTEN ONLY via mute_ledger.clear_dismissal() / clear_dismissals() (loud no-match on an unknown dismissal_seq, idempotent over already-inactive dismissals). References the dismissal by data.dismissal_seq (preferred — the chat_dismissal event's seq) or by data.target_id / data.fingerprint (clears every dismissal with that identity written BEFORE the clear). Readers of chat_dismissal MUST honor it: a dismissal followed by a matching clear is INACTIVE regardless of remaining TTL (mute_ledger.live_mutes / active_dismissal_target_ids are the canonical readers).

commitment_resolved.description: Closes a commitment. WRITTEN ONLY via commitment_state.close_commitment() (Phase 2 Stage B, F2 — the single closure path: id normalization, loud no-match, full-set idempotency, pending_review floor). References the commitment via one of the closer-id aliases (cru_match closer chain): commitment_id~thread_id~id~target_id, or a seq alias (commitment_seq~source_event_seq, F3 amnesty chain). The append gate REJECTS closures carrying none of these (Phase 1). close_commitment writes data.commitment_id (canonical) + resolved_by + evidence (≤200 chars) + resolution (done|dropped|superseded).

commitment_reclassified.description: Kind override marker (Phase 2 Stage D, S6/S5) — additive; the projector applies data.new_kind to the referenced commitment read-side (history never rewritten). Written by the S6 migration script (promise→task partition) and promote_task_to_commitment (task→promise, one-tap promote when a counterparty appears). Never delete/recreate.

commitment_reopened.description: Reopens a closed commitment (Phase 2 Stage D, S4 undo) — additive; the projector honors the LATEST of closure vs reopen in append order. Written by the triage undo path via commitment_state.reopen_commitment.

decision.description: A logged decision. The decision text lives under one of: decision~summary~title.

meeting.description: A meeting record. Has a title or summary.

meeting_processed.description: A processed meeting. References the meeting and carries a summary/title.

interaction.description: A passive-capture touchpoint. Carries a source_ref (dedup key) or a summary.

email_drafted.description: A draft produced by email-writer (event fires from apply-choices on click).

email_sent.description: A sent email; closure event linking back via draft_event_seq. gmail_thread_id (B6) when the send response provides it.

pack_run.description: Audit/telemetry trail of a scheduled-task / orchestrator fire.

pattern_break_detected.description: A person whose contact cadence broke (Pulse). Carries the person and the diagnostic counts.

prep_brief.description: Per-brief prep receipt (v4.5.2 S1). One per Call_Prep brief written, carrying the meeting id — THE signal the morning brief's no-prep detection reads (F-29). Written only by receipts.log_prep_receipt; not a task-run receipt (five briefs in one fire are five prep_brief events and ONE pack_run).

reminder.description: A user-created pin-until-cleared reminder (v4.6.0 W4a). NOT a commitment kind — never enters buckets, counts, chase, or triage. data.origin MUST be 'user_explicit' (gate-enforced; no skill, sweep, or scheduled task may mint one). id minted rem_<ulid> at build/gate time. repeat is 'weekly' | 'monthly' | {"every_days": N} — recurrence lives on reminders, not commitments (M decision 2026-07-09). personal defaults true when the reminder references no tracked business entity; personal reminders render ONLY in M-facing surfaces. ref (optional) points at a commitment/event id for context only — clearing the reminder never touches the referenced item.

reminder_updated.description: Push / keep / edit on an existing reminder. reminder_id REQUIRED (gate-rejected without it — an id-less update is a dead letter). action 'push' carries new remind_from (also re-arms a cleared one-shot); 'keep' is an acknowledged touch that resets the escalation clock; 'edit' revises summary/due. origin MUST be 'user_explicit'.

deal_created.description: A deal thread opened for tracking (SPEC PIPE1). WRITTEN ONLY via deal_state.create_deal / adopt_deal (adopt = attaching a deal object to a pre-PIPE1 kind='deal' thread). data.value present only when the user stated it — never estimated.

deal_updated.description: A non-stage field changed on an open deal (value / expected_close / forecast_category / currency / source). WRITTEN ONLY via deal_state.update_deal; stage moves are deal_stage_changed, terminal outcomes are deal_won/deal_lost. Carries at least one changed field.

deal_stage_changed.description: A deal moved between active stages (SPEC PIPE1; backward moves allowed — deals regress; days-in-stage resets either way). WRITTEN ONLY via deal_state.set_stage.

deal_won.description: Terminal win (SPEC PIPE1). WRITTEN ONLY via deal_state.close_deal(outcome='won') — idempotent; thread status flips to 'resolved'. data.converted_prospect true when the same call atomically ran the prospect->client conversion (D6 — the '[Name] signed' utterance).

deal_lost.description: Terminal loss (SPEC PIPE1). WRITTEN ONLY via deal_state.close_deal(outcome='lost') — a valid loss_reason is REQUIRED (rejected without one); thread status flips to 'archived'. THE 'lost-deal events' board-pack-assembler section 4 reads.

deal_update_proposed.description: PIPE1 Part 2 (registered up front per the wave pattern; no writer until the deal-signal detector ships): a propose-and-confirm deal update surfaced from observed meeting/email signal. Nothing mutates until the user confirms through apply-choices -> deal_state.

deal_update_dismissed.description: PIPE1 Part 2 (registered up front; no writer until the detector ships): the user dismissed a proposed deal update — the cooldown record the detector reads before re-proposing.

brain_proposal.description: A unified Living Brain proposal (SPEC LB1): one uncertain observation a detector wants confirmed (tier confirm) or narrated (tier auto — legal only for AUTO_ALLOWED change classes with a registered reverser; propose() raises otherwise). WRITTEN ONLY via brain_proposals.propose(), which consults proposal_ledger.active_cooldowns (declined-within-60d fingerprints suppressed at source) and dedups on fingerprint against open proposals. action_tuples must map to registered verb_taxonomy action ids (no-consumer proposals rejected at source, D10). Deal-kind proposals additionally write the reserved PIPE1 deal_update_proposed alongside.

brain_proposal_resolved.description: Adjudicates a brain_proposal (SPEC LB1 — the tombstone). WRITTEN ONLY via brain_proposals.resolve_proposal() from apply-choices cr-brain dispatch: user_action in applied|edited|declined|skipped (same vocabulary as proposal_feedback.jsonl — resolve_proposal also appends the ledger row so cooldown math is shared). The projector stops surfacing any proposal_id a tombstone references. declined starts the 60-day fingerprint cooldown.

brain_proposal_expired.description: Silent TTL expiry of an unanswered brain_proposal (SPEC LB1). WRITTEN ONLY by cleanup's expiry sweep via brain_proposals.expire_stale() — logged, never nagged; the count is visible in cleanup's Monday-note card-health line. No cooldown: an expired fingerprint may be re-proposed if the signal persists.

brain_change_undone.description: One reversed change from a Living Brain undo batch (SPEC LB1). WRITTEN ONLY via brain_undo.undo_batch() — the narration-trail marker; the reversal itself is the change class's ADDITIVE reversing event (commitment_reopened, chat_dismissal_cleared, a status->archived person_updated/org_updated), appended by the registered reverser immediately before this marker. change_ref points at the reversed change's audit anchor (event seq or id); reverser names the REVERSERS registry key that ran. Never edits or deletes prior events.

reminder_cleared.description: Clears a reminder. reminder_id REQUIRED. For repeating reminders the reader re-arms to the next occurrence after data.occurrence (defaults to the occurrence active at clear time) — derive-next-on-read, no scheduler. Clearing a reminder with ref NEVER closes the referenced commitment. origin MUST be 'user_explicit'.
